name: Unpatched
what_changed: vkd3d-proton as GE-Proton ships it, no changes

name: Steps 1-5
what_changed: VRAM reserve for render targets; geometry decompression fix; index cache; particle batching; discard barriers; particle draw constants; lazy descriptor heaps

name: Page drops
what_changed: Drops destination pages the engine overwrites anyway, so they are never swapped back in

name: Sparse light grid
what_changed: The 512 MiB light grid is backed only where the engine uses it

name: Index cache fix
what_changed: A full index cache no longer re-scans its whole ring on every draw

name: Sparse skinning buffer
what_changed: The 196 MiB skinning buffer is backed only where the engine uses it

name: Lighting fix + SSD
what_changed: Light grid and skinning backed further up front (no missing lighting); game moved to the SSD so the driver's shader cache works

name: Learned sizes + gates
what_changed: Light grid, skinning buffer, VRAM reserve and budget hold sized from what earlier sessions of this game build actually used, instead of constants tuned on this PC; each feature checks it can help (known game build, a separate GPU, sparse memory support) before changing anything

name: Index cache eviction fix
what_changed: The index cache freed only the first page of each run it evicted, so it refused runs it had room for; now it frees the whole run (refusals 2153/s -> 304/s)

name: Clear keep
what_changed: A full clear of a render target that sits in memory shared with others no longer throws its layout away when vkd3d can prove, in GPU order, that no other resource used that memory since the target last initialized it (about 18 clears per frame); also review fixes to the learned sizes, the integrated-GPU gates and the light grid and skinning growth

name: Render-thread CPU cuts
what_changed: Less locking and fewer driver calls on the game's render thread: draw counts kept per command list, the index cache bound once per command buffer, lock-free fence polling, index cache hits under a shared lock, and a lock-free repeat check in clear keep; nothing the GPU draws changes

name: Open-world index cache
what_changed: In the open world the game copies new geometry into its geometry heap on the GPU, which made S16's index cache turn itself off for the rest of the session; S17 copies those bytes into the cached runs too, so the cache keeps working (byte-for-byte check: 4.3 million cached draws, 0 differ). The fight never does such copies, so it has no fight launches: see Open world
